metadata.description: Epoch-1 deploy intent journal (R8A2): the durable record written atomically BEFORE apply, carrying the plan hash, the prior receipt generation, and every planned resource with its desired digest (campaigns/packages-2026-09 architecture §7.2). Receipt-last alone cannot cover a crash after the first external write; this journal is what recovery reads. It plans state — it never carries secrets, commands or credentials. Generated Rust is the runtime journal type.
Record schema epoch; 1 in epoch 1. The behaviour cell refuses every other value, so a newer journal fails loudly instead of parsing into a wrong meaning.
The hash of the plan this intent executes — exactly 64 lowercase hex, no `sha256:` prefix; validated by the behaviour cell. Recovery joins an intent to its receipt through this hash.
The full identity of the deploy target the plan selected: project, optional package, profile, target id and generation.

Every resource the plan intends to touch, with its desired digest — the exact set recovery compares against, so an empty list is an explicit statement (a plan that touches nothing), never an omission.
The generation of the prior receipt this deploy supersedes; absent for a first deployment with no prior receipt.

A record's timestamp — a JTD `timestamp`, i.e. RFC 3339 on the wire, bound to `chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>` in code (the same binding the shared `timestamp` fragment and `hello`'s `world_sunset` carry). Spelled `"type": "timestamp"` and not `"type": "string"` because a bare string would give a date a SECOND legal spelling in the system, and one thing is written one way. Local to this schema: the record family is its only consumer, and a strict (`foreign_parsers = "none"`) schema must not pull a shared fragment the permissive formats also read.
The identity of one deploy run: which project (and optional package), which profile selected it, which target id ran, and which generation of that target this is.
The project identity; non-blank and control-free; validated by the behaviour cell.
The profile name that selected the target — backend-id grammar `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}`; validated by the behaviour cell.
The deploy target id — backend-id grammar; validated by the behaviour cell.
The generation this intent deploys; 0 is a legal first generation.
The package identity when the deploy comes from one package rather than the host project; non-blank; validated by the behaviour cell.
One planned resource: its identity, the digest the plan wants it at, and the digest the prior receipt recorded (absent when the resource is new).
The resource identity — an owned path or a named resource; non-blank and control-free; validated by the behaviour cell.
The digest the plan wants this resource at — exactly 64 lowercase hex; validated by the behaviour cell.

The digest the prior receipt recorded for this resource — exactly 64 lowercase hex; validated by the behaviour cell. Recovery accepts a resource at either digest; a third digest means concurrent mutation and a refusal.
